clue.text: Elocution class not on for mum

parts.note: elocution is the art of clear speech

indicators.note: not tells you the following word is absent from the phrase for the class

parts.note: a class is a lesson
taken as written

explanation.surface: The public-speaking lesson has been cancelled for Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like Mother but means silent; 'not' takes ON off the end of the phrase for an elocution class.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep mum is to stay silent, saying nothing.

clue.text: Hibernian hospital removed flag

indicators.note: removed says the letter for hospital is taken away from the word before

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: An Irish hospital has taken down its banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner here but a plant: the yellow flag is a waterside flower of this family. 'removed' takes H off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: flag is a common name for several plants of this genus, such as the yellow flag.

clue.text: Female demons edit articles, one about posh cricket club

indicators.note: about puts the editing word and the one around the posh club letters

parts.note: to sub is newspaper slang for to sub-edit copy
U is the old British label for upper-class usage
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: She-devils rewrite pieces, including one on an exclusive cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SUB plus I around UCC. U for posh comes from the British 'U and non-U' labels for upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore these are demons in woman's form that visit sleeping men.

clue.text: Inn landlord initially is hard to put out

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The innkeeper is, at first, difficult to annoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoy or evict, but here it means issue in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to put out a book or statement is to issue it to readers.

clue.text: Current member, previously receiving note, shows weakness

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: receiving says the word for previously takes the note inside it

parts.note: once means formerly
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sitting MP who earlier got a memo reveals a frailty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is not present-day but the symbol for electrical current; 'receiving' puts TE inside ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean powerlessness, a lack of strength to act.

clue.text: Dark disheartened girl, low, retiring

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart of the word, leaving its first and last letters
retiring means going back, so the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A dark-haired, downcast girl, feeling sad and shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the noise a cow makes, not a mood; 'retiring' turns that noise into OOM, and 'disheartened' empties the girl. 'Dark' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: the dark is murk or half-light, as in 'gathering dusk'.

clue.text: Stage school runs system to identify high-fliers

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A drama academy operates a scheme to spot its star pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: The high-fliers are literal aircraft, not gifted students. RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.
explanation.definitionFit: It detects aircraft by bouncing radio waves off them.

clue.text: Unknown egg fancier and animal student

parts.note: Z is one of the letters algebra uses for an unknown
an oologist studies or collects birds' eggs

explanation.surface: An anonymous egg collector who also studies wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of this kind studies animals, the fauna of the world.

clue.text: English flower, say, garden's first seasonal treat

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower
say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word garden's before it

explanation.surface: An English bloom, perhaps, is the garden's earliest delight of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chocolate one is a springtime sweet given at a Christian festival.

clue.text: Corporal remains Catholic priest at heart

indicators.note: at heart places the priest in the middle of the letters for Catholic

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: The army corporal is still, deep down, a Catholic priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal remains' reads as a soldier staying put; it means bodily remains, as kept in a shrine. 'at heart' puts the priest in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's bone or other bodily fragment kept for veneration is one.

clue.text: Supporter relies on transport finally leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the letter just named departs from the word for relies on

parts.note: someone who relies on a friend trusts them

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word transport

explanation.surface: A fan depends on a bus that is at last pulling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks T from transport and 'leaving' drops one T from TRUSTS. The supporter is a framework or surgical support, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a framework holding up a roof or bridge, or a padded surgical belt.

clue.text: Sort of red skin disease covers sick Arab, except for one area

indicators.note: covers says the disease goes around the outside of the rest

parts.note: pox is a disease marked by pustules on the skin
ill means sick

indicators.note: except for one says a single copy of the next letter is left out of the word Arab

explanation.surface: A reddish rash spreads over an ailing Arab, sparing just one patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for one' leaves ARB and 'covers' wraps the disease round the rest. British street postboxes are painted a bright red that takes their name.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the bright scarlet shade of British street postboxes.

clue.text: Wide space for each gold sovereign

parts.note: an em is a printer's space as wide as the type is high
per means for each
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A roomy pouch for every gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold sovereign' looks like the old British coin; split it, and sovereign alone is a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are monarchs, one ruling an empire.

clue.text: Mountain enclave with soldiers and gunmen

parts.note: with can mean and, as in 'fish with chips'
OR is other ranks, the British army term for non-officers
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A highland hideout full of troops and armed men.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'and' is only a join; 'with' supplies the letters AND. OR (other ranks) and RA (Royal Artillery) are British army abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tiny Pyrenean state tucked between France and Spain.

clue.text: He was bound to land somewhat refreshed after spin

indicators.note: after spin says the letters found are turned round to read the other way
somewhat means only part of the word refreshed is used

explanation.surface: A pilot sure to touch down, a little revived once the plane stopped whirling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes FRES from refreshed and 'after spin' turns it round. 'bound to land' means tied to the soil, not certain to touch down.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal labourer was legally tied to his lord's estate.

clue.text: New worker interrupts men in shifts roughly

indicators.note: interrupts says the new worker breaks into the word for men

parts.note: men are males
a hand is a manual worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: A recent recruit butts in on men working approximately in shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' is a verb here, moves, not spells of work; 'interrupts' is the insertion and 'in' merely joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: it means moves something with force and little care.

clue.text: Shiatsu unusual, except at one's local course?

indicators.note: unusual says the remaining letters are put in an unfamiliar order
except says the next word's letters are left out of Shiatsu

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Massage therapy is rare, other than on the class near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' removes AT from Shiatsu, leaving SHISU, which 'unusual' rearranges. 'one' is shiatsu itself: a dish from its homeland, Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is Japanese, so a food from Japan is a dish local to it.

clue.text: Exploits eastern chap regularly wearing black suit

indicators.note: wearing says the chosen letters have the suit around them

parts.note: spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of the word chap

explanation.surface: An oriental fellow who often wears a dark suit is taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' is a noun, adventures, not a verb; the 'black suit' is from a pack of cards, with 'regularly' and 'wearing' doing the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are daring adventures or reckless stunts.

clue.text: Retaliation rule in haberdashery?

definitions.meaning: an action taken in response to an opponent's move
whimsically, a yardstick kept on the serving top of a draper's shop for gauging cloth

explanation.definitionFit: One reading is a response to a threat; the other, split in two, is a ruler on a shop's serving top.

clue.text: German polymath not originally in foreign currency business

parts.note: lei is the plural of leu, the money of Romania

indicators.note: in says the single letter sits inside the currency and business taken together

parts.note: biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A learned German who did not start out trading foreign exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the philosopher and mathematician who co-invented calculus.

clue.text: Drink more bubbly in general perhaps

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing agitation, so the letters of more are stirred about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Have extra champagne, as a rule maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more bubbly' reads as extra champagne; 'bubbly' rearranges MORE into REMO. 'in general' hides a military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a top army commander is one kind of overall chief.

clue.text: It may charge money

definitions.meaning: a horned African beast known for running at intruders

explanation.definitionFit: The horned beast attacks at a run, and its name is old British slang for cash.

clue.text: Drawing different matches starts to impress crowd

indicators.note: different says the letters of matches take another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the two words after it

explanation.surface: After drawn games, a run of varied fixtures begins to thrill the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests tied matches; it is a diagram. 'different' rearranges MATCHES into SCHEMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a simplified diagram, such as a wiring plan.

clue.text: Regroup in a body after work and come again

indicators.note: after work says the preceding letters have been worked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: Colleagues gather together once the shift ends, then return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after work' rearranges all of REGROUP IN A BODY. 'come again' is the colloquial request to repeat something.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both are polite ways of asking someone to repeat what they said.

clue.text: Hire data about old society in units of 24

indicators.note: about says the hire and data words go around the letter for old

parts.note: to hire is to rent
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Lease records concerning a former association, in batches of two dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 points to the answer at 24 down, the hospital beams measured in these; 'about' is the insertion and the surface's two dozen is a blind.
explanation.definitionFit: They are the old units of exposure to the radiation named at 24 down.

clue.text: Intolerant NKVD chief, one promoted in the fifties, pursuing one

indicators.note: pursuing says the rest follows after the final one of the clue

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in says the altered name sits inside the run of fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, here three of them

indicators.note: promoted, in a down clue, lifts a letter higher up the name

parts.note: Lavrenti Beria ran Stalin's secret police, the NKVD
the Roman numeral for one is I, the letter that moves

explanation.surface: A bigoted secret-police boss, elevated in the 1950s, hunts an individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' lifts the name's I to the top, giving IBERA; 'in' sets that among three fifties, the whole 'pursuing' the last one. The surface nods to his real fall in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean narrow-minded, opposed to freedom of opinion.

clue.text: Stores piano in monument, topped and tailed

indicators.note: in says the letter for piano goes inside the trimmed monument
topped and tailed removes the first and last letters of the word for monument

parts.note: a memorial is a monument to the dead
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a piano inside a statue with both its head and base cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' leaves EMORIA from MEMORIAL and 'in' places P inside it. 'Stores' is a noun, shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: they are large shops selling a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Giant pig eats dog all up

indicators.note: all up, in a down clue, says the whole assembly is read from the bottom
eats says the pig word swallows the dog word

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to dog someone is to tail them, to follow closely

explanation.surface: An enormous pig devours the whole dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to follow, not the animal; 'eats' builds HTAILOG and 'all up' turns the lot over.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: he is the Philistine colossus felled by David in the Bible.

clue.text: Attachment to sole stimulant

definitions.meaning: the part of a shoe above the bottom, stitched to it
slang for a pep pill such as an amphetamine

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the top part of a shoe and slang for an amphetamine pill.

clue.text: Lift caught under cross beams in hospital

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, places the heard word below the cross

parts.note: a cross is the shape of the letter X

indicators.note: caught means heard by the ear, so the word for lift is taken by its sound

parts.note: to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: An elevator is trapped beneath the crossing girders at the infirmary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' means heard: RAISE is said as RAYS, placed 'under' X. The beams are radiation, not girders.
explanation.definitionFit: They are the penetrating radiation a radiography department uses for imaging.
